title: Terminal Portfolio
name: terminal-portfolio
blurb: A replica of the Claude Code terminal UI you drive from the keyboard.
long:
One self-contained HTML file. No build step, no dependencies, no framework. It boots like a real session: welcome box, types `whoami`, a thinking spinner with elapsed seconds, then a selection list you drive with ↑↓, j/k, number keys, Enter and Tab.

The prompt underneath takes real commands: help, ls, cat, open, stack, contact, mcp, clear.

title: Bug Tracker MCP
name: bugtracker-mcp
blurb: Public MCP server over a bilingual issue tracker. No auth.
long:
Most MCP servers stop at tools. This one serves 11 tools, addressable bug:// resources, and server-provided prompts. Bilingual Hebrew and English full-text search, binary image return over MCP, and a nightly self-reseed so the demo data never rots.

Add it to Claude in one click. No key, no account.

title: Multi-Tenant SaaS
name: multi-tenant-saas
blurb: Government-audited restaurant platform on the Cloudflare edge.
long: Government-approved, continuously audited multi-tenant SaaS on Cloudflare Workers, D1, R2 and Durable Objects. Architected, shipped and operated solo. The fiscal-compliance layer is built in-house rather than bought in.

title: Agent Workspace
name: agent-workspace
blurb: Parallel builders, blind review rounds, staged approval gates.
long: Parallel builders on isolated lanes, blind review rounds, staged approval gates. Plus an LLM-queried knowledge base an engineering team uses to recover the reasoning behind a decision, which the diff never records.

title: sukarfleet
name: sukarfleet
blurb: One AI agent across all your machines. Source and releases are public.
long:
One AI agent across all your machines. A small daemon on each machine keeps the agent's memory, workspace and notes in sync, so it picks up where it left off whichever keyboard you sit at.

It replicates git repositories rather than copying files, so history survives and a conflict is a real merge. There is no central server to lose.

Public since September 2026, AGPL-3.0 for the daemon and MIT for the client edges. Linux is the tested platform and runs a real two-machine fleet every day. macOS and Windows are implemented and barely tried, which the project says out loud rather than burying.

release.headline: The daemon, the mesh transport and the tray console, installed by one command.
release.commandNote: Debian and Ubuntu. It clones the tag into ~/.local/share/sukarfleet/app and runs the quickstart from that checkout, so the thing installing you is a repository you can read first. Nothing in this stage needs root, and it prints the one command that does.

platforms.note: The installer fetches this for you and checks it against a pinned SHA256. Take the file directly to verify that hash yourself, or to put the console on a machine by hand. There is no aarch64 build yet.

Unzip it and double-click install/windows/Add-To-Fleet.cmd. Both stages ran on a Windows 11 VM on release day. The admin lane cannot elevate here because Windows has no sudo, so the installer switches it off and you drive admin from a Linux machine.
The quickstart is systemd-only, so a Mac is a manual install from this archive. Everything except privilege elevation is implemented and nobody on the project owns a Mac to try it on.

title: Claude Chat Bridge
name: claude-chat-bridge
blurb: Web chat UI over live Claude Code sessions.
long:
A web chat UI wired into interactive Claude Code sessions over the official channel transport, with multi-thread conversations and inline HTML artifacts. No API token, no separate credit pool. It drives the sessions you already have.

The running bridge lives at chat.raceus.co.il behind Cloudflare Access.

title: sukartask
name: sukartask
blurb: Task tracker shared across agent sessions.
long: Named task sets shared across Claude Code sessions, so work in progress on one machine stays visible from another, and from a phone. Per-user auth, self-hosted behind access control.

title: sukarplan
name: sukarplan
blurb: The artifact board. Every plan an agent writes, readable from a phone.
long: Agents publish standalone HTML artifacts here instead of leaving them as files on one machine. Highlight a passage to comment; the agent replies on that same passage.

title: T3 Code
name: t3-code
blurb: A full coding environment in the browser, from any device.
long: Browser-based coding against the real fleet machines, behind Cloudflare Access.

title: SSH Gateway
name: ssh-gateway
blurb: Shell into the anchor machine through Access.
long:
An SSH ingress, not a web app. The Access application in front of it accepts a service token, not a browser login, so nothing here opens in a tab.

Connect with `ssh ssh.raceus.co.il` through cloudflared. This card documents the connection rather than pretending to open it.
